LESSON: HAJJ

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.4: Hajj

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Hajj. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are the prerequisites for the performance of Hajj?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each
2. describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity
3. appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: HAJJ
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Hajj helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: HAJJ
Study Hajj like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each

What this means
In this part you learn to explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Hajj” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Hajj in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Hajj is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Hajj” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Hajj in your own words. (skill: describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Hajj to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each.
3. Practise this skill: describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate Hajj as a pillar of Islam.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Hajj from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Hajj: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Hajj?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the prerequisites for the performance of Hajj?
2. What is the significance of Hajj?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Hajj means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain different types of Hajj to fulfil the requirements for each.
5. Be able to: describe the procedure of performing each type of Hajj for its validity.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
